  ## Introduction
  
#  This analysis uses natural language processing (NLP) in R to explore 10 internship job descriptions related to data analytics, data science, and data engineering. The objective is to identify frequently occurring terms and examine similarities in word usage through hierarchical and K-means clustering.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 7
)
```

## 1. Load Packages and Text Files

```{r load-data}
# Load required packages
library(tm)
library(SnowballC)
library(ggplot2)
library(wordcloud)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(cluster)

# Set directory containing internship descriptions
cname <- file.path("jobs_text")

# Confirm that the directory exists
stopifnot(dir.exists(cname))

# List text files
text_files <- list.files(
  cname,
  pattern = "\\.txt$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

basename(text_files)

# Confirm that 10 text files are available
stopifnot(length(text_files) == 10)

# Import text documents into a corpus
docs <- Corpus(
  DirSource(cname, pattern = "\\.txt$")
)
```

## 2. Text Preprocessing

#The documents are cleaned by removing punctuation, numbers, common English stopwords, and unnecessary whitespace. Stemming is applied to reduce words to common roots.

```{r preprocessing}
# Convert text to lowercase
docs <- tm_map(docs, content_transformer(tolower))

# Remove punctuation and numbers
docs <- tm_map(docs, removePunctuation)
docs <- tm_map(docs, removeNumbers)

# Remove special characters left from job descriptions
docs <- tm_map(
  docs,
  content_transformer(function(x) {
    gsub("[^[:alnum:][:space:]]", " ", x)
  })
)

# Remove common English stopwords
docs <- tm_map(
  docs,
  removeWords,
  stopwords("english")
)

# Reduce words to their stems
docs <- tm_map(docs, stemDocument)

# Remove extra whitespace
docs <- tm_map(docs, stripWhitespace)
```

## 3. Document-Term Matrix and Frequency Analysis

#The document-term matrix represents the frequency of terms within each job description. Sparse terms are removed to focus on terms appearing across multiple documents.

```{r term-matrix}
# Create document-term and term-document matrices
dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(docs)
tdm <- TermDocumentMatrix(docs)

# Convert the original DTM into a matrix
m <- as.matrix(dtm)

# Display the original matrix dimensions
dim(m)

# Remove sparse terms
dtms <- removeSparseTerms(dtm, 0.8)

# Convert filtered DTM to a matrix
m2 <- as.matrix(dtms)

# Display filtered matrix dimensions
dim(m2)

# Calculate term frequencies
freq <- colSums(m2)

# Sort frequencies in descending order
freq <- sort(freq, decreasing = TRUE)

# Display the 20 most frequent terms
head(freq, 20)

# Find terms occurring at least twice
findFreqTerms(dtm, lowfreq = 2)
```

## 4. Word-Frequency Bar Chart

#The bar chart displays the 20 most frequently occurring terms across the internship job descriptions.

```{r word-frequency, fig.height=7}
# Create a data frame containing the top 20 terms
wf <- data.frame(
  word = names(head(freq, 20)),
  frequency = as.numeric(head(freq, 20))
)

# Generate word-frequency bar chart
ggplot(
  wf,
  aes(
    x = reorder(word, frequency),
    y = frequency
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 20 Words in Data Internship Job Descriptions",
    x = "Terms",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Word Cloud

#The word cloud provides a visual representation of the most frequently occurring terms, with larger words representing higher frequencies.

```{r word-cloud, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# Select color palette
dark2 <- brewer.pal(6, "Dark2")

# Generate word cloud
set.seed(123)

wordcloud(
  words = names(freq),
  freq = freq,
  max.words = 100,
  random.order = FALSE,
  rot.per = 0.2,
  colors = dark2
)
```

## 6. Hierarchical Clustering

#Hierarchical clustering is used to examine similarities in the frequency patterns of the 20 most common terms across the job descriptions.

```{r hierarchical-clustering, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# Select the 20 most frequent terms
top_terms <- names(head(freq, 20))

# Create a term-by-document matrix
term_matrix <- t(
  m2[, top_terms, drop = FALSE]
)

# Calculate Euclidean distances
d <- dist(
  term_matrix,
  method = "euclidean"
)

# Perform hierarchical clustering
hc <- hclust(
  d,
  method = "ward.D2"
)

# Generate dendrogram
plot(
  hc,
  main = "Hierarchical Clustering of Internship Job Description Terms",
  xlab = "Terms",
  sub = "",
  cex = 0.8
)

# Highlight five clusters
rect.hclust(
  hc,
  k = 5,
  border = 2:6
)
```

## 7. K-Means Clustering

#K-means clustering groups the selected terms into two clusters based on similarities in their frequency patterns across the internship descriptions.

```{r kmeans-clustering, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# Use the term matrix from hierarchical clustering
k_data <- term_matrix

# Perform K-means clustering
set.seed(123)

kfit <- kmeans(
  k_data,
  centers = 2,
  nstart = 25
)

# Display cluster assignments
kfit$cluster

# Generate K-means cluster plot
clusplot(
  k_data,
  kfit$cluster,
  color = TRUE,
  shade = TRUE,
  labels = 2,
  lines = 0,
  main = "K-Means Clustering of Internship Job Description Terms"
)
```

## 8. Conclusion

#The NLP analysis explores the most recurring terms in 10 data-related internship descriptions. Word-frequency analysis and the word cloud highlight recurring concepts, while hierarchical and K-means clustering examine similarities in how terms are distributed across the documents.

#The results provide a way to explore patterns in the language employers use when describing technical responsibilities, qualifications, and professional expectations.
